newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended down across the board on Monday on profit-taking from retail investors, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 3,390 yuan ($409) per tonne, losing 18 yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 3,380 yuan and hit a high of 3,400.
May fell five yuan to 3,360, September 29 to 3,415, November 50 to 3,395 and the January 1998 contract 40 to 3,400.
Combined volume fell to 14,100 tonnes from 15,300.
Soybeans opened lower and fell further on profit-taking before short-covering emerged to push prices off their lows, traders said.

"Profit-taking from retail investors dominated today's trading due to a lack of short-term positive news," one trader said. "Investors continued to move hot money into the stock markets, which are more active."
Traders said they expected soybeans to consolidate in a narrow range with most investors sidelined due to a lack of market-moving news.
